rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God reveals the Qur’an gradually to train its hearers and answer each objection as it arises.
rows.anchor: أي بالتدريج للتدريب وللجواب عن كل شبهة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is the finest discourse and greatest remembrance; only God’s revelation makes it unsurpassable, and no human could match it even for a day.
rows.anchor: ولولا أنه هو الذي نزله لما كان الأحسن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The noun “book” apposes “best” and describes a revelation that gathers every good.
rows.anchor: { كتابا } أي جامعا لكل خير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Qur’an is alike throughout in miraculous eloquence and sound admonition, with no discrepancy in wording or meaning despite descending in parts over more than twenty years; human speech inevitably varies.
rows.anchor: لا تفاوت فيه أصلا في لفظ ولا معنى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording avoids متشبها, which could suggest the text is unclear in meaning and thus not praiseworthy.
rows.anchor: لئلا يظن أنه غير واضح الدلالة لا يمدح به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Mathānī means repeated: stories, admonitions, rulings, and wisdom recur in varied forms and with varied degrees of evidential clarity, without contradiction in their basic meaning.
rows.anchor: أي تثنى فيه القصص والمواهظ والأحكام والحكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The repeated material pairs opposites; each explicit promise or warning also intimates the consequence of its opposite, presenting both sides twice.
rows.anchor: فلا ترتب على شيء من ذلك جزاء صريحا إلا ثني بإفهام ما لضده تلويحا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows an alternative parse, تقديره متشابهة مثانيه, with مثانيه in the accusative as specification.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون التقدير : متشابهة مثانيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Repetition suits souls resistant to admonition: what is not reiterated does not take root or produce its effect; hence the Prophet repeated statements three times or more.
rows.anchor: ومن ثم كان النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يكرر قوله ثلاث مرات فأكثر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although repetition can weary, the Qur’an grows sweeter and more delightful through repeated recitation, even across night and day.
rows.anchor: أنه يطرب مع التكرار , ويزداد حلاوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The word means to shiver, gather, and contract intensely; he derives it from القشع, described as dry, aged fat.
rows.anchor: أي تهتز وتتجمع وتتقبض تقبضا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The added and repeated consonant intensifies the meaning and signals emphatic recurrence.
rows.anchor: واختير حرف التكرير إشارة إلى المبالغة فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The skins are the body’s outer surfaces; those who fear God fear intensely and take a delight that produces reverence.
rows.anchor: أي ظواهر أجسام { الذين يخشون } أي يخافون خوفا شديدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their fear of their beneficent Lord heightens their praise: recollection of divine majesty makes them more fearful.
rows.anchor: وزاد في مدحهم بأنهم يخافون المحسن

rows.speaker: النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم
rows.claim: A report from the Prophet says that when a servant’s skin shivers from fear of God, his sins fall away; al-Ṭabarānī transmits it from al-ʿAbbās, with no grading stated.
rows.anchor: روى الطبراني عن العباس رضي الله عنه أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم قال

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: ابن عمر
rows.claim: Ibn ʿUmar saw an Iraqi collapse when Qur’an and God’s remembrance were recited, objected that God-fearing believers do not collapse, attributed it to Satan, and said this was not the Companions’ practice.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عمر رضي الله عنهما أنه مر برجل من أهل العراق ساقط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the shiver, skins soften and hearts follow; the ordering moves from the dryness implied by gooseflesh back to hope, while keeping hearts away from any suggestion of hardness.
rows.anchor: وقدم ما صرح فيه بالاقشعرار الذي يلزمه البيس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fear is located only in the heart, so the verse does not explicitly say that hearts shiver; this avoids wording that might imply hardness.
rows.anchor: وكان سر حذف التصريح بذلك تنزيها عن ذكر ما قد يفهم القسوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition إلى conveys that the restless, changeable heart settles and becomes tranquil in God’s remembrance.
rows.anchor: دل على حفظه له بنافذ أمره وباهر عظمته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s remembrance fundamentally evokes hope, because His mercy preceded His wrath.
rows.anchor: فإن الأصل في ذكره الرجاء لأن رحمته سبقت غضبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The explicit name replaces a pronoun to prevent misidentifying its antecedent as the Lord in a way that could support unionist or other heresies; “remembrance of God” also magnifies the passage over “discourse” or “book.”
rows.anchor: وأظهر موضع الإضمار لأحسن الحديث لئلا يوهم أن الضمير للرب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling it God’s remembrance rather than merely discourse or book gives it greater dignity and shifts from the attribute of beneficence to the comprehensive divine name.
rows.anchor: بل عدل إلى ما عرف أنه ذكره سبحانه ليكون أفخم لشأنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ذلك points to the wondrous revealed discourse and the bodily contraction and release it produces; this is God’s guidance.
rows.anchor: أي الأمر العظيم الغريب من الحديث المنزل والقبض والبسط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The same revelation guides some and misleads others: hardened hearts remain unmoved, so what guides one person becomes misguidance for another.
rows.anchor: ومن هداه الله فما له من مضل

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the sovereign God firmly misleads someone, no guide can redirect him because none can overturn God’s command or judgment.
rows.anchor: لأنه لا راد لأمره ولا معقب لحكمه

words: يهدي به من يشاء ومن يضلل الله
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse uses ellipsis by correspondence: God’s unrestricted guiding implies the parallel action of misleading, and the stated impossibility of guiding the misled implies its omitted counterpart for the guided; the argument refutes the Qadariyya.
rows.anchor: ذكر أولا إطلاق أمره في الهداية دليلا على حذف مثله في الضلال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After contrasting the expanded and constricted breast and concluding that one is guided and the other astray, the passage unfolds each group’s outcome in a deliberately interwoven interrogative; misguidance leads to punishment and guidance to bliss.
rows.anchor: شرع في بيان ما لكل منهما نشرا مشوشا في أسلوب الإنكار أيضا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The singular follows the form من so the wording does not suggest that the faces are those of leaders; the face becomes a shield because the hand, normally used to ward off danger, is bound, and the honored face must protect the rest of the body.
rows.anchor: وأفرد على لفظ { من } لئلا يظن أن الوجوه الأكابر

words: يتقي بوجهه سوء العذاب يوم القيامة
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoer is thrown upside down into Hell, bound, with no free limb to shield his face; a mountain-like sulfur stone hangs at his neck and he is dragged face-first, unlike the one who receives bliss in heart and body.
rows.anchor: لأنه يرمي به في النار منكوسا وهو مكبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive وقيل fits the general character of reproach; the text could have said “to him,” but instead names the wrongdoers and uses the plural to generalize the judgment and show their numbers do not help them.
rows.anchor: ولما كان مطلق التوبيخ والتقريع متكئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers are those who abandoned guidance, followed desire, and went astray while leading others astray.
rows.anchor: أي الذين تركوا طريق الهدى واتبعوا الهوى فضلوا وأضلوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are told to taste the recompense of what they used to regard as the benefit and fruit of their deeds and conduct.
rows.anchor: أي جزاء ما { كنتم تكسبون * } أي تعدونه فائدة وثمرة لأعمالكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By ellipsis through correspondence, the opening question implies the omitted counterpart, and the words addressed to wrongdoers imply that the righteous are told to be content and take delight as recompense for their deeds.
rows.anchor: ذكر الاستفهام أولا دليلا على حذف متعلقه ثانيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the unbelievers expect only immediate, worldly particulars, like unreasoning animals, the warning turns to punishment in this life and answers the implied question whether they will be punished here.
rows.anchor: لا ينتظرون إلا الجزئيات الحاضرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition من signals how near the earlier punished peoples were in time; he gives Saba and Tubbaʿ and their peers as examples, then notes that their precautions did not save them.
rows.anchor: أي مثل سبأ وقوم تبع وأنظارهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples’ punishment arrived from an unforeseen direction, and their caution did not avail them.
rows.anchor: وكان أمرهم علينا يسيرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The righteous receive whatever they wish at their Lord, the beneficent and gentle, because they yielded to His will in this life and He fulfills their wishes in the next.
rows.anchor: لأنهم سلموا له في الأولى ما يشاء , فسلم لهم في الأخرى ما يشاؤون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: This great reward is for everyone characterized by ihsan as they were by piety; God loves them, and the author describes their closeness through the language of their hearing, sight, hand, and foot.
rows.anchor: فأحبه اللهي سبحانه كما أحبهم

words: ليكفر الله عنهم أسوأ الذي عملوا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person of ihsan keeps the gravest sins before him and works to undo them; this is why the verse describes the reward as covering their worst deeds.
rows.anchor: كان المحسن من جعل أكبر ذنوبه نصب عينيه وعمل على هدمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses ليكفر as “to cover greatly,” and allows its explanatory clause to give the reason either for the people’s ihsan or for their reward.
rows.anchor: أي يستر سترا عظيما كأنه قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shift to the name Allah after the attribute of beneficence signals strenuous worship and that only the unrestricted sovereign can forgive whom He wills.
rows.anchor: وعبر بالاسم الأعظم لفتا عن صفة الإحسان إشارة إلى عظيم الاجتهاد في العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They confessed their error and repented with remorse, cessation, and resolve not to return; when the greater sin is erased, the lesser is erased too, as good deeds remove bad deeds.
rows.anchor: وتابوا عند بالندم والإقلاع والعزم على عدم العود وقد علم أنه إذا محي الأكبر انمحى الأصغر لأن الحسنات يذهبن السيئات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After cleansing their evil, God brightens them with good; because He increases and nurtures righteous deeds, the added ب signals that He makes all their good works like the best of them.
rows.anchor: زاد الجار في الجزاء إعلاما بأنه يجعل الأعمال الصالحة كلها مثل أعلاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He prefers الذي here because this sūra’s focus is narrower than al-Naḥl and الذي and من are less ambiguous than ما; the relative clause refers to the deed, in an expression like “a silver ring.”
rows.anchor: وكانت ( الذي ) و ( من ) أقل إبهاما من ( ما )

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The construction with كانوا and the imperfect indicates that their good works recur over time and are deeply habitual.
rows.anchor: وأشار إلى مداومتهم على الخير بالتعبير بالكون والمضارع

rows.speaker: القشيري
rows.claim: Al-Qushayrī argues that the best works must receive the best reward, that the best reward is seeing God, and therefore the vision must be perpetual; the author calls this a strong inference.
rows.anchor: قال القشيري , ثم يجب أن يكون على أحسن الأعمال أحسن الثواب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the unbelievers deny the truth and threaten the Prophet with their idols, the verse’s emphatic question affirms God’s sufficiency and denies that He fails to protect His servant.
rows.anchor: حسن كل الحسن قوله مقرا للكفاية غاية الإقرار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The servant is the one devoted purely to God, without associating anything with Him, whom God aids against his opponents until His religion prevails and he needs no other protector.
rows.anchor: أي الخالص له الذي لم يشرك به أصلا كما تقدم في المثل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Trust in God’s sufficiency does not rule out using worldly means: God may connect effects to them or render them ineffective, and using means best accords with His wise ordering of the world.
rows.anchor: وهاذ لا ينافي السعي في الأسباب مع اعتقاد أنها بيد الله

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر
rows.claim: Ḥamza, al-Kisāʾī, and Abū Jaʿfar read عباده in the plural, meaning the Messenger and his followers.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي وأبو جعفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their threat echoes the people of ʿĀd, who told Hūd that some of their gods had afflicted him; the author says later feminizing the idols will add to their humiliation.
rows.anchor: وسيأتي التعبير عنهم بالتانيث زيادة في توبيخهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone determines guidance and misguidance; this consoles the Prophet against grieving over those he cannot guide and rejects the Qadariyya position.
rows.anchor: فقال مخففا عنه صلى الله عليه وسلم في إذهاب نفسه عليهم حسرات دامغا للقدرية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God may make one cause bring misguidance to some, warranting punishment, and guidance to others, bringing blessing; He can still guide some of the present opponents if He wills.
rows.anchor: جعل شيئا واحدا سببا لضلال قوم ليكون ضلالهم في الظاهر علة للنقمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God is irresistible in carrying out His will and can exact revenge by subjecting His target to what grieves and humiliates him, or by blinding him to the clearest light and leading him astray.
rows.anchor: أي غالب لما يريد في إضلاله قوما يدعون أنهم النهاية في كمال العقول

none: The segment contains only quoted verse text and no commentary.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links the unexpected punishment with the promise that no soul knows what God has hidden for believers of joy in 32:17; what they never imagined is more painful to the wrongdoers.
rows.anchor: بحسب جبلاتهم وما فطروا عليه من الإهمال والتهاون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The punishment was beyond what their habits and nature allowed them to expect or even consider; that makes it harsher on the soul and more terrifying to the heart.
rows.anchor: لم يكن في طبائعهم أن يعتمدوا أن يحسبوه وتجوزه عقولهم من العذاب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: بدا means that their evil deeds appeared fully, as though exposed in an open plain with nothing concealing them.
rows.anchor: أي ظهر ظهورا تاما كأنه في البادية لا مانع منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the ransom context, kasb is more specific than work: it denotes the essence or concentrated yield of an action; al-Ashʿarī therefore made acquisition the basis of recompense, and the offenders’ choicest works are lost, much less their lesser ones.
rows.anchor: عبر هنا بالكسب الذي من مدلوله الخلاصة والعصارة التي هي سر الشيء فهو أخص من العمل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: حاق means that something surrounds them with inevitability and harm.
rows.anchor: أي أحاط على جهة اللزوم والأذى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: What surrounds them is the Fire and all the things they were warned about, which they persistently mocked.
rows.anchor: يطلبون ويوجدون الهزء والسخرية به من النار وجميع ما كانوا يتوعدون به

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He explains the shift to this example by their strange habit of repaying beneficence with evil, though they ought to do the opposite.
rows.anchor: وهو مجازاة الإحسان بالإساءة وقد كانوا جديرين بضده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: الإنسان generalizes the pattern to the human type, and ضر means any harm, including harm from a source one would expect; he links the wording to the opening of this sūra.
rows.anchor: أي ضر كان من جهة يتوقعها كما تقدم في التي في أول السورة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He allows the example to follow either the preceding ransom scene or the unbelievers’ aversion to mentioning God: despite their dislike of His remembrance and delight in idols, distress makes them call on Him alone.
rows.anchor: ويجوز أن يكون مسببا عن الإخبار بافتدائهم بما يقدرون عليه وأن يكون مسببا عن اشمئزازهم من توحيد الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In distress they call God, recognizing His greatness rather than their idols, even though they recoil from mention of Him and rejoice when idols are mentioned; most people acknowledge truth only under harm.
rows.anchor: عالما بعظمتنا دون آلهته مع اشمئزازه من ذكرنا واستبشاره بذكرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The delayed ثم signals the severity and duration of the harm, making his quick forgetfulness of it especially blameworthy.
rows.anchor: أشار إلى عظمته وطول زمنه بأداة التراخي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God grants the blessing out of sheer beneficence, cares for him, and makes it fit his condition despite his having done nothing to earn it.
rows.anchor: أي أعطيناه على عظمتنا متفضلين عليه محسنين القيام بأمره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing comes entirely from God; no one else has any share in it.
rows.anchor: ليس لأحد غيرنا فيها شائبة من ولولا عظمتنا ما كانت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He forgets even prolonged hardship, appropriates the gift to himself, and does not learn to thank its giver; the masculine pronoun magnifies the blessing.
rows.anchor: ناسيا لما كان فيه من الضر وإن كان قد طال أمده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passive verb signals that he does not care to identify or thank the giver; he attends instead to the gift’s greatness and his own self-importance.
rows.anchor: وبنى الفعل للمجهول إشارة إلى أنه لا نظر له في تعرف المعطي من هو يشكره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He claims the great gift is proportionate to his own greatness, as though he gives to himself according to his own measure.
rows.anchor: لأني عظيم فأنا أعطي على مقداري

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He parses ما as an added particle that blocks إن and gives an exclusive sense; alternatively, ما is a relative pronoun as the subject of إن, with على علم as its predicate.
rows.anchor: و ( ما ) هي الزائدة الكافة لأن للدلالة على الحصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the alternative parse, he says the gift came through great knowledge earned by effort, seeking, and scheming, or through God’s knowledge that he deserved it.
rows.anchor: وجد مني بطريق الكسب والاجتهاد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The blessing is instead a trial that tests gratitude against ingratitude and establishes the proof; if it leads to Hell, it is a form of gradual entrapment.
rows.anchor: لاختباره هل يشكر أم يكفر لتقام عليه الحجة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The feminine pronoun belittles the gift relative to God’s power and its outcome of delusion, whereas the earlier masculine pronoun had magnified it as something deserving gratitude.
rows.anchor: وأنث الضمير تحقيرا لها بالنسبة إلى قدرته سبحانه وتعالى ولأنها أدت إلى الغرور بعد أن ذكر ضميرها أولا تعظيما لها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most of these speakers acquire no knowledge because they are innately coarse and ignorant; even if God answered their call in Hell and blessed them, they would credit someone else as they do in this life.
rows.anchor: فلو أنهم إذا دعونا وهم في جهنم أجبناهم وأنعمنا عليهم نعمتنا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Quraysh are the main intended audience, though the statement covers earlier and later peoples too; people before them made the same claim about receiving wealth through knowledge.
rows.anchor: ولما كان كفار قريش مقصودين بهذت قصدا عظيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He links their boast to Qarun’s claim and to those who approved his state and wished for his wealth.
rows.anchor: كما قال قارون ومن رضي حاله فتمنى ماله

words: فما أغنى عنهم ما كانوا يكسبون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The earlier peoples’ repeated accumulation of wealth and status, even on a vast scale, could not benefit them or avert God’s decree.
rows.anchor: أي يجددون على الاستمرار كسبه من المال والجاه وإن كان مليء السهل والجبل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their acquisitions brought them their evil consequences and painful recompense.
rows.anchor: أي وبال ذلك وما يسوء من آثاره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers among the present audience are the Prophet’s people, who fail to ponder the Qur’an; had they pondered its signs, they would have known, but blindness had already overtaken them.
rows.anchor: أي قومك الذين لا يتدبرون القرآن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The current wrongdoers are surely to suffer the consequences of their arrogant, heedless deeds in this world and the terrors prepared for the next; the author says the warning began with Badr and continued thereafter.
rows.anchor: من وقعة بدر ثم ما تبعه إلى ما لا آخر له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the sūra denies knowledge to most people and stresses that God fulfills His promise, it says “know” here; certainty that God knows is enough, unlike the earlier wording in al-Rum.
rows.anchor: وكان مقصود السورة بيان أنه صادق الوعد ومطلق العلم كاف فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The evidence is what they have seen over their lifetimes and learned through experience.
rows.anchor: أي بما رأوا في أعمارهم ومن التجارب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Naming Allah here magnifies the matter and closes off ambiguity and obstinate argument.
rows.anchor: ولفت الكلام إلى الاسم الأعظم تعظيما للمقام ودفعا للبس والتعنت بغاية الإفهام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God alone expands provision to whomever He wills, even someone without ability or means.
rows.anchor: أي هو وحده { الرزق } غاية البسط { لمن يشاء } وإن كان لا حيلة له ولا قوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God can constrict provision with hardship for the most resourceful and politically powerful; if distribution were not His alone, bodily strength and knowledge would prevent anyone from being poor.
rows.anchor: أي يضيق مع النكد بأمر قاهر على من هو أوسع الناس باعا في الحيل وأمكنهم في الدول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: If provision were not controlled by God alone, people with bodily strength and knowledge would never be poor.
rows.anchor: لولا أن ذلك كله منه وحده لما كان أحد ممن له قوة في الجسم وتمكن في العلم فقيرا أصلا

words: إن في ذلك لآيات لقوم يؤمنون
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although no one denies God’s control of provision, the signs benefit people prepared to renew faith that all affairs belong to Him, so they fear, hope, and give thanks; those prepared for the Fire gain no benefit from them.
rows.anchor: أي هيئوا لأن يوجد منهم الإيمان فيجددوا التصديق في كل وقت تجديدا مستمرا
